summary: Focus on low glycemic index foods. Limit refined carbohydrates and added sugars. Prioritize fiber-rich foods that slow glucose absorption.
mealTips: Pair carbohydrates with protein or healthy fat to slow glucose absorption
Choose whole grains over refined grains at every meal
Include fiber-rich vegetables in every meal to buffer blood sugar spikes
Eat consistent portion sizes at regular meal times to maintain stable blood glucose
Use cinnamon, fenugreek, and turmeric as blood-sugar-friendly seasonings
Opt for berries over tropical fruits for natural sweetness with lower glycemic impact

summary: Manage protein, potassium, phosphorus, and sodium intake. Limit high-potassium and high-phosphorus foods. Avoid processed and preserved foods high in sodium.
mealTips: Limit protein portions to reduce kidney workload — prefer egg whites over whole eggs when reducing protein
Leach high-potassium vegetables by peeling, cutting small, and boiling in large water volume
Avoid salt substitutes as they typically contain potassium chloride which raises blood potassium
Choose fresh or frozen vegetables without added salt over canned varieties
Use fresh herbs, lemon juice, and vinegar as low-sodium flavor boosters
Monitor fluid intake as recommended by your nephrologist

summary: Reduce high-purine foods that increase uric acid production. Stay well hydrated. Limit alcohol and fructose-rich foods. Favor plant proteins over animal proteins.
mealTips: Drink at least 8 glasses of water daily to help flush uric acid through the kidneys
Eat cherries or drink tart cherry juice — compounds in cherries lower uric acid levels
Choose low-fat or non-fat dairy products which actively lower uric acid excretion
Limit serving size of meat to 85-100g per meal and spread protein across the day
Replace red meat with chicken breast or plant proteins like tofu and eggs
Avoid fasting as rapid weight loss can trigger gout attacks by increasing uric acid

summary: Follow a DASH-style diet: rich in fruits, vegetables, whole grains, and low-fat dairy. Strictly limit sodium, saturated fat, and added sugars.
mealTips: Target less than 1500mg sodium per day — use herbs, spices, and lemon as flavor substitutes
Increase potassium intake from whole foods like bananas, sweet potatoes, and leafy greens to counteract sodium
Use the DASH diet framework: 4-5 servings of vegetables and fruits per day
Choose unsalted nuts over salted snacks — the magnesium in nuts supports blood pressure control
Cook at home to control sodium levels — restaurant and processed foods are often very high in salt
Reduce alcohol consumption as it directly raises blood pressure in excess
